loop: gauntlet: a builder and a separate critic with fresh context per piece. The critic runs ours next to native, names the biggest gap, and the piece loops until the critic picks ours.
bar: native APFS (this Mac) and ext4 (moonscape): cargo build and git status within 1.5x, pjdfstest + fsx + xfstests-generic no worse than native, zero data loss in crash-injection.

items.title: #1 dedup ratio on the real worktree corpus
items.detail: Full run on 45 slots, 843,889 files, 273.43 GiB raw, 0 errors. Raw 1.00x, per-file zstd 3.60x, whole-file dedup 3.12x, CDC only 5.08x, CDC + zstd 14.04x. A median extra lumen slot costs 0.47 GiB compressed (4.9% of raw). Caveat: 97.5% of raw is cargo target/ and 91.7% is one repo, so 14x is a Rust build-output result. Write-up: docs/spikes/1-dedup-corpus.md. Gate met.

items.title: #2 mmap and file locking over the macOS NFS loopback
items.detail: Viable without sudo (-o locallocks). 24/24 checks. Tuned server: clean builds 0.9x-1.2x native, git status 1.3x-1.4x, warm and incremental builds 2.5x-3.5x (misses 1.5x, see #18). Old server was 3-5x clean and 9-55x warm because of nfsserve bugs (LINK, tracker lock, readdir cookie), fixed in the vendored copy (#19). One 60-dep crate, passthrough server, n=3-5. Write-up: docs/spikes/2-nfs-loopback.md.

items.title: #3 build and git status overhead versus native
items.detail: macOS NFS: clean builds 0.9x-1.2x, warm 2.5x-3.5x. Linux FUSE passthrough in an OrbStack VM (btrfs native): clean 1.03x-1.14x, edit rebuild 1.16x-1.19x, no-op 1.07x-1.48x, seeded first build 1.1x, all within 1.5x. Bulk metadata (git status, find, rm, cp) 2x-3x. Gap looks macOS-NFS-specific (#18). Passthrough only, no ext4 numbers, 7.8k-file tree. docs/spikes/2-nfs-loopback.md and 3-linux-fuse.md

items.title: #4 .git inside the filesystem
items.detail: Reads fine with .git on the mount (status 1.3x, log 1.1x). Writes: add -A 3.9x, commit 3.9x; native .git overlay gives 1.1x and 1.7x. Checkout 9-11x, worktree add 11x, cold status 6.6x in both layouts (working-tree file ops). Found and fixed a write race on read-only-mode files; one unexplained corrupt idx (#21). Large-repo n=3-5, load 15-62. docs/spikes/4-git-inside-the-filesystem.md

items.title: #5 treehouse process detection on the mount
items.detail: cwd-only detection works on the mount for every detectable case. Gap: a process holding an open fd or flock after chdir out is not detected, and on the mount the reset leaves a .nfs silly-rename file and a dirty slot while return exits 0 (#20). lsof and cwd lookup fine. Real pools untouched. docs/spikes/5-treehouse-process-detection.md

items.title: #6 artifact byte-identity across slots at different paths
items.detail: Independent debug slots cost 12.8%-28% of slot 1 after dedup, 1.8% release. Remapping or CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 brings it under 3%. Clone-seeded plus one edit: 8.8%-10.3%. Slot-specific remap makes a copied target dirty. Mount namespaces (#17) not needed for dedup on these crates. Two small crates, one run per cell. docs/spikes/6-artifact-byte-identity.md

items.title: #18 decision: warm and incremental builds 2.5x-3.5x over NFS loopback
items.detail: Option 1 experiment running: attribute the round trips on the macOS NFS loopback, then try mount options and server-side cache priming. Linux FUSE evidence in the issue suggests the gap is macOS NFS specific.

items.title: #19 v1 server requirements and nfsserve fixes
items.detail: LINK, tracker lock, readdir cookie (fixed in vendored copy); open: symlink SETATTR, AppleDouble policy, stale nlink in readdir, memory growth, readdir sort, path map.

items.title: #20 v1: open-fd holders not detected, .nfs dirt on the mount
items.detail: Propose upstream fd detection to treehouse, add a cowfs control-API process list, decide how .nfs entries are handled.

items.title: #21 v1: data integrity - corrupt idx unexplained, readdir cookie
items.detail: Write race fixed and regression-checked. Corrupt idx not reproduced, needs a soak on the fixed server. Readdir cookie still position-based.

items.title: PR #22 spikes 1-6 (draft)
items.detail: Draft PR with all spike write-ups. Base of the v1 stack: #23 skeleton, then #24 store and #25 meta.

items.title: #7 chunking, hashing and block store
items.detail: Builder is writing docs/v1-store.md, then the block store with crash-injection, corruption and model-based tests and a benchmark on real data. A separate critic reviews after. Worktree ~/.treehouse/cowfs-7c1bf8/1, branch v1/7-block-store.

items.title: #8 Merkle tree and O(1) writable snapshots
items.detail: Built together with #9 in one crate. Design note first (docs/v1-meta.md): hardlinks need an inode layer, a pure Merkle tree cannot express them. Worktree ~/.treehouse/cowfs-7c1bf8/2, branch v1/8-9-meta.

items.title: #9 redb metadata store with crash consistency
items.detail: redb with a crash-injection harness (custom StorageBackend and kill -9 rounds) checked by a consistency verifier.

items.title: #10 garbage collection
#11 Linux FUSE mount
items.detail: Thin FUSE adapter over Vfs with the spike 3 defaults (long TTLs, negative cache, keep_cache). Mount tests run in the OrbStack VM. Worktree slot 5, branch v1/11-fuse.

items.title: #12 macOS NFS loopback mount
items.detail: Vendored and fixed nfsserve plus a Vfs adapter, mount management with locallocks, the spike batteries as ignored mount tests. Worktree slot 6, branch v1/12-nfs.

items.title: #13 CLI and Unix-socket control API
items.detail: docs/v1-control-api.md first, then cowfs-ctl (protocol, client, server) and the cowfs CLI against a stub backend with a Backend seam for the real core. Worktree slot 7, branch v1/13-cli.

items.title: #14 cowfs import (non-destructive migration)
#15 treehouse mode (a) transparent
#16 treehouse mode (b) snapshot-native slots and warm base
#17 Linux mount namespaces for canonical paths
#29 cowfs-vfs trait, MemVfs and conformance suite
items.detail: Trait and types done (PR #27). MemVfs plus a generic conformance suite with mutation checks are being built. Every backend must pass the suite. Worktree slot 4, branch v1/vfs-test.

items.title: #26 cowfs-core: Vfs over store and meta
items.detail: The layer the original plan lacked: file IO, write-back cache, re-chunking, open-handle tracking, snapshot namespace. Starts when the store, meta and conformance suite land.

items.title: cargo build within 1.5x of native (APFS and ext4)
items.detail: Linux FUSE passthrough: builds within 1.5x (1.03x-1.48x). macOS NFS: clean builds within, warm/incremental 2.5x-3.5x (#18). Real backend not measured.

items.title: git status on a large tree within 1.5x of native
items.detail: macOS NFS git status 1.3x-1.4x (--ignored 1.7x-1.8x). Linux FUSE git status 2.75x on 7.8k files (22ms vs 48ms). Large tracked repo not measured.
